Particular attention must be paid to the negative moment capacities of the yield lines radiating from the column capitals when determining E. Top bar cut-offs, if present, will reduce the moment capacity on the part of the yield line furthest from the column. In addition, corner effects must be considered where the two walls intersect. That is, as a result of the increased stiffness at the corners, the ultimate moment of the reinforcement is reduced to 2/3 of its capacity over a length equal to ½ the length of the positive yield line.
